name: Salamanca
summary: After weeks of manoeuvring side by side, Marmont stretched his army out to the west to cut Wellington off from Portugal. Wellington saw the gap open, sent Pakenham's 3rd Division into the head of the French column and Leith's 5th and Le Marchant's heavy dragoons after it, and broke the Army of Portugal in an afternoon; Clausel's counter-attack was stopped and the French were routed.

sources.label: Battle of Salamanca order of battle (Wikipedia)

forces.name: Pakenham's 3rd Division
forces.summary: Sent by Wellington himself to cut across the head of the French column, it fell on Thomières's division on the march and broke it, opening the battle.
notes: The list allows one Highland or Light battalion in four, so a brigade of three may have none; where one had a Highland or Light regiment, that shows as a historical departure.
Wellington gave Pakenham his orders in person, so the book's named Wellington leads it here; Pakenham commanded the division.
The order of battle gives the Portuguese regiments but not their battalions; each is one of the list's regiments.
Batteries are spread among the divisions; the order of battle lists them under the army's artillery without saying which served with which.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Sir Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington, with his own rating.

forces.name: Leith's 5th Division
forces.summary: Advanced in two lines over the crest against Maucune's division, which had formed square against the cavalry, and broke it with a volley and the bayonet; Leith was wounded.
notes: The order of battle gives the Portuguese regiments but not their battalions; each is one of the list's regiments.
Each brigade had a company of the Brunswick Oels; one is shown, the list allowing one in an army.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Cole's 4th Division
forces.summary: Attacked Clausel and Bonet in the centre and was thrown back by Clausel's counter-attack; Cole was wounded.
notes: The order of battle gives the Portuguese regiments but not their battalions; each is one of the list's regiments.
Ellis's company of the Brunswick Oels is left out.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Clinton's 6th Division
forces.summary: Wellington's reserve, sent in to stop Clausel's counter-attack; it held, at heavy cost, and drove on against Ferey's rearguard as night fell.
notes: The order of battle gives the Portuguese regiments but not their battalions; each is one of the list's regiments.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Campbell's 1st Division
forces.summary: Held the allied left near the Lesser Arapile and joined the pursuit late in the day.
notes: Wheatley's brigade had two Highland battalions, the 42nd and 79th, where the list allows one in four, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Hope's 7th Division
forces.summary: In reserve behind the allied left, with the King's German Legion and Brunswick light troops.
notes: De Bernewitz's brigade had two Light battalions in three where the list allows one in four, which shows as a historical departure.
The order of battle gives the Portuguese regiments but not their battalions; each is one of the list's regiments.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Light Division
forces.summary: On the far left, facing Foy, it pressed the French right as the army broke and harried the retreat.
notes: The list allows horse artillery by the cavalry taken, so a horse troop with an infantry division shows as a historical departure.
Two Light Brigades where the list takes one show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Pack's and Bradford's Portuguese
forces.summary: Pack's brigade stormed the Greater Arapile and was thrown off it by Bonet's men; Bradford's came in on the right with Leith.
notes: The order of battle gives the Portuguese regiments but not their battalions; each is one of the list's regiments.
Without British brigades for the Portuguese ones to go with, the list's ratio shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Le Marchant's and Bock's Heavy Dragoons
forces.summary: Le Marchant's brigade rode into Maucune's and Brenier's broken battalions and destroyed eight of them in the most successful British cavalry charge of the war; Le Marchant was killed at its head.
notes: Cavalry on its own has no infantry brigades for its brigades to go with, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Anson's, Alten's and D'Urban's Cavalry
forces.summary: D'Urban's Portuguese and the 14th Light Dragoons led the attack on the head of the French column with Pakenham; Anson's light dragoons covered the left.
notes: Cavalry on its own has no infantry brigades for its brigades to go with, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Thomières's Division
forces.summary: Leading the French march west, it was caught strung out on the road by Pakenham and D'Urban and broken; Thomières was killed.
notes: The 23rd Léger, its other regiment, was absent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Maucune's Division
forces.summary: Formed square against the British cavalry, it was broken by Leith's volley and then ridden down by Le Marchant's dragoons.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Brenier's Division
forces.summary: Coming up to support Maucune, it was caught by Le Marchant's charge as it formed and swept away.
notes: The Régiment de Prusse, only remnants by then, is a Small battalion.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Clausel's Division
forces.summary: Clausel took command of the army when Marmont and Bonet were wounded, and his division led the counter-attack that threw back Cole and Pack before Clinton's 6th Division stopped it.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Bonet's Division
forces.summary: Held the Greater Arapile, throwing Pack's Portuguese off it, and joined Clausel's counter-attack; Bonet was wounded.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Ferey's Division
forces.summary: Formed the rearguard as the army broke, standing in line against Clinton's division until nightfall to cover the retreat; Ferey was killed.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Sarrut's Division
forces.summary: Following behind Thomières and Maucune, it came up too late to help them and joined the retreat.
notes: The 130th Ligne, its other regiment, was absent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Foy's Division
forces.summary: On the French right facing the Light Division, it held together through the rout and covered the retreat to the Tormes.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Curto's and Boyer's Cavalry
forces.summary: Curto's light horse was scattered with Thomières's division; Boyer's dragoons tried to cover the retreat.
notes: Several of these regiments had only one or two squadrons; the 28th Chasseurs (one squadron) could be Small. Cavalry without the infantry brigades it's allowed by shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.
